items.title: Emotional eSafety boss says Jewish community let down by 'loose guardrails'
items.description: eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant became emotional while apologising to Jewish victims of social media harassment who do not meet the regulator's legal threshold for intervention.

items.title: PM's tennis match shows property tax fight isn't over
items.description: A mortgage broker forked out $16,500 on Canberra’s night of nights to take his grudge about budget tax directly up to the prime minister in a tennis match at the Lodge.

items.title: Christian Brothers granted pause on abuse victim payouts
items.description: The Christian Brothers religious order has been granted a moratorium on all civil claims against it, after arguing it was running out of money to pay victims of child sexual abuse.

items.title: 'Robbing people using visas': Applicants shocked by sudden price hike
items.description: International students and families say they feel shocked and exploited after visa fees across dozens of categories rose on July 1 without warning, with some surging more than 200 per cent.

items.title: Privacy Commissioner ordered to hand over report on Amex security failures
items.description: The Privacy Commissioner has been ordered by parliament to hand over a secret report detailing its investigation into American Express's technology security failures, after using gag orders and legal threats to keep it confidential.

items.title: Micro 'cockroach' drones help find earthquake survivors in Venezuela
items.description: A week after devastating twin earthquakes struck Venezuela rescue teams are using drones, dogs, cameras and specialised listening equipment to search for survivors.

items.title: Gina Rinehart and estranged kids to pay bulk of legal costs after royalties trial
items.description: Mining billionaire Gina Rinehart and her two estranged children will have to pay the lion's share of the legal costs of a mammoth trial that determined the payment of royalties from some of Australia's most lucrative iron ore mines, a WA judge has ruled.

items.title: NDIS fraud 'gaps remain open' as integrity report handed down
items.description: A Labor-led parliamentary inquiry into fraud in the NDIS has made 12 recommendations to improve the integrity of the scheme.

items.title: Pictures show interior of Trump's new Air Force One jet
items.description: The jet, gifted to the US government by Qatar, has been retrofitted, with Trump shaking off concerns over the cost.

items.title: Teen accused of abducting 17yo with intent to force marriage
items.description: A teen has been accused of abducting a 17-year-old girl from near a Melbourne school with the intention of forcing her to marry him.

items.title: MP's company fined $555k over worker's quad bike death
items.description: The court heard the 82-year-old worker was not wearing a helmet and the quad had no rollover protection when the crash occurred.

items.title: Venezuelans make desperate pleas for help a week after devastating double earthquake
items.description: Venezuelans in the coastal city of La Guaira are pleading for heavy machinery to assist in ongoing rescue operations more than a week after a double earthquake devastated the area. Magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes devastated the area one week ago and at least 2,200 people have died.  People on the ground have faced a desperate wait for help to find family members lost under the rubble. Frustration is growing in the community as they ask where the government is, and why help has not arrived.

items.title: Live: Cats face Lions in blockbuster clash at Kardinia Park
items.description: Geelong and Brisbane meet at Kardinia Park for a spot in the top four, as round 17 of the AFL kicks off under lights. Follow live.

items.title: 'At greatest risk of CTE': Expert calls out dangers of heading the ball
items.description: With all eyes on the World Cup, Australian football's management of the risks associated with the practice of heading the ball, such as dementia and CTE, is in the spotlight.

items.title: Nobody knows where John Frum came from but he is god in this village
items.description: On Vanuatu's Tanna Island, I immerse myself in a culture that worships a shape-shifting spirit known as John Frum.

items.title: Jackass began with a gunshot. Now it's a $500m franchise
items.description: For more than 25 years, prank franchise Jackass has been delighting teens and terrifying parents. Now the gang is heading to the cinemas for what could be their last ride.

items.title: Matthew Flinders’s steamy letters reveal a hidden side to the man who named Australia
items.description: Flinders circumnavigated and named Australia. Impressive stuff, but he also wrote many impassioned letters and lived a life full of crushes.

items.title: Quick hits: Feuding Belgians save the day, England claims 'disadvantage'
items.description: Belgium stars turn on each other before combining to save their team, England makes claims of "disadvantage", and Congo's goalkeeper gives it all he's got. Here are today's World Cup quick hits.

items.title: Australia ranks third-highest for median wealth globally, UBS data shows
items.description: Australia holds the third-highest median wealth globally at $306,074, pipped at the post by Luxembourg and Belgium.

items.title: Ex-Sydney childcare worker jailed for 'disturbing and depraved' child abuse
items.description: A painstaking victim identification process was undertaken by Australian Federal Police to establish his offending occurred at six of out-of-school hours care centres over a three-year period.

items.title: Catholic Schools NSW chief to stand aside amid corruption probe
items.description: The head of the body governing the state's catholic schools will stand aside after he was named in a corruption probe investigating donations to the NSW Liberal Party.

items.title: Financial misconduct compensation scheme faces $170m cost blowout
items.description: The First Guardian and Shield super disasters, and Dixon Advisory fallout, is causing a cost blowout in the taxpayer-funded scheme that is designed to compensate victims of financial misconduct.

items.title: Former St Mary's Hostel site recognised as key Stolen Generations place
items.description: Former residents say the permanent heritage listing of the St Mary's Hostel site in Alice Springs is an important step towards healing, truth-telling and remembering the children taken there under assimilation-era policies.

items.title: Major milk company fined for misleading consumers about fresh milk
items.description: One of Australia's largest milk providers has been fined by the consumer watchdog for misleading consumers with "fresh milk" labels on products that contained substantial amounts of powdered milk.

items.title: Why F1's rumour mill is speculating futures of Piastri and Verstappen
items.description: F1's rumour mill has been in overdrive in recent times about Oscar Piastri's future at McLaren, with his boss having to hose down suggestions the Australian will be driving anything other than a Papaya-coloured F1 car in 2027.
